extracted.intended_audience: educated general readers and persons seeking to cultivate manners and social conduct (gentlemen, hosts, social leaders)
extracted.subtask_description: An essayistic prescription on the qualities, behaviors, and social principles that constitute the 'gentleman' and good manners — aimed at cultivating presence, taste, and social efficacy in company and public life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal force / original energy
rubrics_metrics.description: Power first, or no leading class. ... the name will be found to point at original energy. It describes a man standing in his own right and working after untaught methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A gentleman must have native energy and courage — 'the bold fellow whose forms are not to be broken through' — able to take the lead in war, politics, trade, or social life. Examples cited: Saladin, Julius Caesar, Alexander. Antipattern: timid, merely ceremonious persons without initiative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Truth and lordship of one's actions
rubrics_metrics.description: The gentleman is a man of truth, lord of his own actions, and expressing that lordship in his behavior, not in any manner dependent and servile, either on persons, or opinions, or possessions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courtesy and all forms of good-breeding rest on truth and frankness. A gentleman does not dodge; he meets others frankly and assures them of his presence and character. Antipatterns: skulking, dissimulation, servility to persons or opinions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good‑nature / benevolence / generosity
rubrics_metrics.description: Beyond this fact of truth and real force, the word denotes good‑nature or benevolence: manhood first, and then gentleness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sympathy, heartiness, and willingness to oblige are essential. Real social success requires warmth and an ability to make others comfortable (examples: Fox's generosity; rescuers, founders of charities). Antipatterns: selfish intellect without sympathy; unpleasant egotism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Taste and perception of beauty
rubrics_metrics.description: We imperatively require a perception of, and a homage to beauty in our companions. ... Accuracy is essential to beauty, and quick perceptions to politeness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A cultivated sense of proportion, accuracy, and beauty refines manners: know what is fit and fair, avoid coarse behavior, and prefer measured expression. Antipatterns: the sloven, the boisterous, or those who 'scream' or use excess.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure / moderation / composure
rubrics_metrics.description: If you wish to be loved, love measure. ... All that fashion demands is composure and self-content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Self‑control, moderation of feeling and expression, and composure in company are valued above flashy extremes. Being calm and proportioned permits one to make one's own forms; excess heat or haste offends. Antipatterns: quarrelsomeness, egotistical excess, hurriedness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deference and stately courtesy
rubrics_metrics.description: The complement of this graceful self-respect ... is deference. I like that every chair should be a throne, and hold a king.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A certain stateliness and deference — treating others with reserved honor — preserves dignity in relations. Maintain respect without excessive familiarity; treat domestic and ceremonial roles with appropriate solemnity. Antipatterns: excessive familiarity that erodes distinction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain individuality and guarded intimacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Let us sit apart as the gods, talking from peak to peak all round Olympus. ... The island of a man inviolate. Lovers Should guard their strangeness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preserve personal solitude and a degree of strangeness even in intimacy; do not collapse individuality into over‑familiarity. Antipatterns: surrendering all privacy, blurring personal boundaries through excessive sameness or dependence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manners as facilitation of fellowship
rubrics_metrics.description: Manners aim to facilitate life, to get rid of impediments and bring the man pure to energize. They aid our dealing and conversation ... by getting rid of all avoidable obstructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good manners are instrumental: they remove frictions so people can interact smoothly. Cultivate forms that promote easy, agreeable intercourse. Antipatterns: behaviors that create needless misunderstanding or obstruction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fashion as selector and guard against pretenders
rubrics_metrics.description: To say what good of fashion we can, it rests on reality, and hates nothing so much as pretenders; to exclude and mystify pretenders ... is its delight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fashion and elite circles operate as selection mechanisms: they reward real merit and exclude affectation. One should respect the root that fashion often signals authentic social qualities, while recognizing its frivolous side. Antipatterns: shallow imitation and believing fashion equals true worth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid bringing business‑precision into social life
rubrics_metrics.description: One may be too punctual and too precise. He must leave the omniscience of business at the door, when he comes into the palace of beauty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not apply the exacting habits of commerce or professional omniscience to convivial settings; allow some freedom and softness in social exchange. Antipatterns: pedantry, hyper‑precision that kills conviviality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presence and mastery of the household / hospitality
rubrics_metrics.description: No house, though it were the Tuileries or the Escurial, is good for anything without a master. ... a gentleman who received a visit, though it were of his sovereign, should not leave his roof, but should wait his arrival at the door of his house.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A host should be visibly the master of his domain: personal presence, responsibility for hospitality, and open reception are marks of true breeding. Antipatterns: hiding behind decorations or screens; letting possessions mask absence of character.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frank recognition and civil introduction
rubrics_metrics.description: As the first thing man requires of man is reality, so that appears in all the forms of society. We pointedly, and by name, introduce the parties to each other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Introduce people clearly, make eye contact, and signal mutual recognition; these straightforward acts establish trust and reality in social relations. Antipatterns: evasive introductions, avoiding direct acknowledgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sympathy, heartiness, and the ability to 'fill' the company
rubrics_metrics.description: The secret of success in society is a certain heartiness and sympathy. ... The favorites of society ... are able men ... contented and contenting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be genuinely pleased in company: supply felicitous remarks, adapt to occasions (weddings, funerals, balls, juries) and make presence beneficial for all. Antipatterns: social awkwardness, inability to respond gracefully to varying situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid egotism; be adaptable across classes
rubrics_metrics.description: Society will pardon much to genius and special gifts, but ... it hates quarrelsome, egotistical, solitary, and gloomy people; ... If the aristocrat is only valid in fashionable circles and not with truckmen, he will never be a leader in fashion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: True gentlemanliness includes a wide affinity that transcends cliques: be able to fraternize with different kinds of people and not rest solely on narrow status. Antipatterns: exclusive snobbery, inability to converse with those outside one's class.

rubrics_metrics.name: Courageous public action and beneficence
rubrics_metrics.description: There is still ever some admirable person in plain clothes, standing on the wharf, who jumps in to rescue a drowning man; ... some absurd inventor of charities; some guide and comforter of runaway slaves ... these are the centres of society.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Heroic deeds, public service, and selfless acts (charity, rescue, civic improvement) are central sources of true social leadership and the creation of worthy fashion. Antipatterns: mere ceremoniousness without substantive benevolent action.
